title: Netflix Streaming Architecture
description: Learn how Netflix delivers video to over 260 million subscribers using microservices, Open Connect CDN, transcoding pipelines, and recommendation systems.

data.text: Netflix streams over 250 million hours of video daily to more than 260 million subscribers across 190 countries. Its architecture is a masterclass in microservices, global CDN, and asynchronous media processing. Understanding Netflix teaches how to build systems that must be always available.

Netflix operates Open Connect, a globally distributed network of cache servers embedded in ISP networks. When you play a video, it streams from the nearest Open Connect node rather than Netflix's central servers. This reduces latency and eliminates cross-continental bandwidth costs.

data.title: Why Netflix Built Its Own CDN
data.text: Netflix spends over $1 billion annually on content delivery. By building Open Connect, Netflix reduced transit costs by 50% and improved streaming quality. The CDN now serves over 15% of all internet traffic.

When a studio delivers a master file, Netflix's transcoding pipeline converts it into multiple resolutions and bitrates. A 2-hour movie might generate 25-30 renditions. Transcoding is CPU-intensive and happens asynchronously, typically within hours of upload.

Netflix runs over 700 microservices. The API gateway routes requests to services like recommendations, playback, billing, and user management. Each service is independently deployable and fault-isolated. Chaos Monkey randomly kills instances to ensure resilience.

terms.definition: Netflix's custom CDN consisting of cache servers deployed inside ISP networks worldwide.
Converting a single master video file into multiple resolutions and bitrates for adaptive streaming.
Netflix's resilience tool that randomly terminates production instances to ensure services recover automatically.

data.title: Netflix Architecture Lessons
points: Custom CDN gives Netflix control over delivery quality and cost
Asynchronous transcoding separates upload from playback readiness
Microservices with fault isolation prevent cascading failures
Adaptive bitrate streaming adjusts quality to network conditions
Chaos engineering is mandatory for resilient systems
data.takeaway: Netflix proves that building custom infrastructure at scale is justified when it gives you competitive advantages in cost, quality, or reliability.

data.title: Design an Adaptive Streaming Protocol
data.description: Design a protocol for adaptive bitrate streaming. The client should be able to switch between 5 quality levels within 2 seconds of network change. Specify the segment duration and buffer strategy.
data.expectedOutcome: 2-4 second segments with a 30-second buffer. Client monitors download speed and switches quality proactively. HLS or DASH manifest provides available renditions.
